chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A group of people came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'Peace be upon you, O our Lord!' So he asked them to repent, but they did not repent. So he dug a pit for them and kindled a fire in it, and dug another pit beside it, and connected them. So when they did not repent, he cast them into the pit and kindled the fire in the other pit until they died.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.يَا رَبَّنَا: O our Lord (phrase used by the group)

ai.seo_question: What was the penalty imposed by Imam Ali (AS) on those who called him 'Lord' and refused to repent?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the judicial precedent set by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) for the penalty of apostasy (riddah) and claiming divinity, specifically illustrating the method of execution by fire. The detail of digging a second, empty pit connected to the first serves to distinguish this specific punishment from general burning, ensuring the fire was contained to the body rather than consuming the entire earth, a nuance valued in Shia fiqh. It underscores the severity of rejecting the Imamate and the divine right of the Prophet's successor.
